evidence: Read of test_release_workflow_pins.py:174-189: the enclosing test is test_h_wheel_and_sdist_test_jobs_with_probes and line 186 is `for probe in ("import rebar", "rebar --help", "rebar-mcp --help", "_build_info"): assert probe in wt` — a presence check on CI-job YAML text, not an output comparison

Separately verified the byte-identical OUTCOME is actually true: every MCP_ENV_VARS entry at mcp_server.py has `"deprecated": False` (37 hits), so the `(deprecated alias)` suffix at mcp_server.py:684 never renders — removing it changes nothing on the wire. The defect is the mis-grounded PROBE citation, not the claim itself.
findings.finding: The acceptance criterion claims `rebar-mcp --help` output is 'byte-identical to before' and cites `tests/unit/test_release_workflow_pins.py:186` as the proving probe, but that line only asserts the literal string 'rebar-mcp --help' is present in the wheel-test CI job YAML (`for probe in (...): assert probe in wt`); it does not capture, run, or byte-compare the `--help` output. The cited probe does not verify the asserted property.

scenarios: Reviewer or implementer trusts line 186 as the regression guard for --help output and ships a change that alters the --help env listing; the cited test still passes because it only checks the invocation string is present in CI YAML.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the parenthetical with a reference to a snapshot test that invokes the --help entrypoint and compares output bytes; alternatively, since all MCP_ENV_VARS entries are deprecated=False and the suffix never renders, state the AC as 'no --help env line changes (the (deprecated alias) suffix is currently unreachable)' and drop the line-186 citation.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify in the Approach that inline_schema must (a) rewrite every 'common.schema.json#/$defs/X' ref inside hoisted defs to the local pointer '#/$defs/X' and (b) transitively hoist all defs reachable from the named schemas (not just directly-referenced ones), so the inlined schema is truly self-contained for jsonschema.validate.
evidence: common.schema.json:62,93,94,148,152 — $defs contain intra-file refs e.g. '"relation": { "$ref": "common.schema.json#/$defs/relation" }', 'citations': items '$ref common.schema.json#/$defs/citation'
ticket_state.schema.json refs e.g. common.schema.json#/$defs/dep and /comment which are themselves composite defs
Plan's self-containment test ('no $ref contains .json#') is an after-the-fact gate, not a mechanism spec; the Approach text names only a top-level hoist and $schema/$id drop
findings.finding: inline_schema's description does not specify rewriting cross-file ref prefixes inside hoisted $defs nor transitively closing over refs that hoisted defs themselves contain; common.schema.json $defs reference each other (dep->relation, comment->citation), so a naive top-level-only hoist leaves unresolvable 'common.schema.json#/$defs/*' refs.
findings.location: Approach — 'inline_schema(names, kind) hoists common.schema.json#/$defs/* into local $defs and drops $schema/$id'
scenarios: A tool whose schema references common 'dep' or 'comment' is advertised; inline_schema hoists 'dep' but leaves its inner '$ref: common.schema.json#/$defs/relation' unrewritten, so jsonschema.validate in the lowlevel call_tool path fails to resolve and every structured result errors at call time.
findings.suggested_fix: State the transitive-closure + prefix-rewrite contract explicitly: 'inline_schema walks all $refs reachable from the named schema(s), copies each referenced common.schema.json#/$defs/X into local $defs/X, and rewrites every common.schema.json# prefix (including those nested inside hoisted defs) to a bare #/$defs/ pointer; repeat to a fixpoint since hoisted defs reference further defs.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Record the exact mcp SDK version against which fn_metadata.output_schema/output_model/wrap_output were confirmed, and note whether these are public API or private internals (pinning the dependency or adding a version guard if private).
evidence: Plan quote: 'sets mcp._tool_manager.get_tool(name).fn_metadata.output_schema, asserting output_model is not None and wrap_output == (kind != "object") so a mis-declared kind fails at startup'

resolve_symbol returned UNRESOLVED for output_schema/output_model/wrap_output on FuncMetadata (these are runtime attributes, so UNRESOLVED is not disproof — but it means the public-API status is unconfirmed)

The lowlevel outputSchema validation claim IS corroborated by retrieved sources (deepwiki modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk 'Output validation: If Tool.outputSchema is defined, validates structured content'; chatforest 'jsonschema.validate(result.structured_content, tool.output_schema)') — so the public contract is verified; the private FuncMetadata attribute names are the only unresolved capability assertion.
The mcp.tool rebinding mechanism itself is established in-repo precedent (_mcp_errors.py:77-133 install_error_guard), so that pattern is not novel.
findings.finding: The plan depends on non-public FastMCP internals (mcp._tool_manager.get_tool(name).fn_metadata.output_schema, .output_model, and .wrap_output) but does not resolve the capability against a specific pinned SDK version, leaving these private-attribute assertions as an unverified version-coupled assumption.

scenarios: An SDK minor/patch upgrade renames or restructures fn_metadata/FuncMetadata, so install_canonical_output_schemas raises AttributeError at startup across all 53 schema-bearing tools.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify why OUTPUT_SCHEMAS_BY_TOOL must be a standalone registry rather than deriving its schema-name mapping from (or co-locating the wrapping-kind data with) the existing schemas.OUTPUT_SCHEMAS, or add a test asserting the two registries agree on every shared tool/command key.
evidence: Plan: 'New src/rebar/_mcp_schema.py (about 220 LOC): OUTPUT_SCHEMAS_BY_TOOL: dict[str, tuple[tuple[str, ...], Literal["object","array","list_of"]]].'

schemas/__init__.py:329 comment calls OUTPUT_SCHEMAS 'The authoritative map of every structured ... output to its schema' and already carries MCP-tool keys (ready.mcp, plan_review_status, get_workflow_status, grounding_info).
The new map adds only the wrapping-kind (object/array/list_of) and multi-name anyOf info on top of the schema-name mapping the existing registry already holds.
findings.finding: The plan introduces a second tool->schema registry (OUTPUT_SCHEMAS_BY_TOOL in _mcp_schema.py) that lives parallel to the existing command->schema registry schemas.OUTPUT_SCHEMAS, without explaining why the two cannot be unified or why they will not drift. The existing OUTPUT_SCHEMAS already keys MCP-tool-named entries (e.g. ready.mcp, plan_review_status, get_workflow_status) to schema names.
scenarios: A tool's canonical schema is renamed or re-keyed in schemas.OUTPUT_SCHEMAS but the parallel OUTPUT_SCHEMAS_BY_TOOL is not updated, so the advertised wire schema silently diverges from the documented output contract.
